name: Cursor agent (Instant Grep, formerly semantic search; terminal sandbox)
language: Tool calls and shell commands (no documented code mode)
engine: Shell on the user's machine; optional sandbox: Seatbelt via sandbox-exec (macOS), Landlock + seccomp (Linux). Search: Instant Grep, a local index.
how_run: Not run: Cursor is not installed and scriptable here. All entries from docs and Cursor blog posts.

P1.detail: No code-calls-tool bridge documented; the agent calls tools directly.

P3.detail: Sandboxed commands: "Network: Blocked by default, then opened by your network mode and sandbox.json." The default network mode is "sandbox.json + Defaults" ("Cursor's built-in defaults for common package managers and language tools"). Whether example.com is in that default list was not checked.

P4.detail: Read access default is System: "The agent can read files outside the workspace without approval. This is the default." Workspace mode restricts sandboxed commands to the workspace, a read allowlist and system paths.

P5.detail: Docs list variables Cursor injects (CURSOR_SANDBOX, CURSOR_ORIG_UID, ...) but do not say whether host secrets are stripped.

P8.detail: Shell state between commands not documented. In Workspace read mode the private temp folder "keeps its files between commands".

P9.detail: No code-level parallel tool calls. The Explore subagent "executes many parallel searches" as agent tool calls.

P12.detail: Real shell on the host; the sandbox is OS-level. "Some commands need full system access and bypass the sandbox. Cursor will indicate when a command runs outside the sandbox and ask for your approval."

source_notes.finding: Current docs: "Cursor ships with Instant Grep, a custom search engine that outperforms ripgrep on large codebases"; "Instant Grep builds and queries its index on your machine. Cursor does not upload file paths or code to build a search index, and it does not store embeddings of your codebase for search."

Forum posts from accounts that speak for Cursor (staff status not verified) say semantic indexing was turned down in 2026: "Semantic/embeddings indexing is being turned down in favor of grep-based retrieval." and "Search runs against the files on your machine, so Cursor no longer builds a semantic index of the repo." (v3.12 onwards). Read only as search excerpts.

The Nov 6, 2025 post measured +12.5% average accuracy (6.5% to 23.5%) with semantic search added to grep and concluded "Semantic search is currently necessary to achieve the best results, especially in large codebases."

macOS: Seatbelt via sandbox-exec with a generated profile for the whole subprocess tree. Linux: Landlock + seccomp; ignored files overwritten in an overlay. Kernel too old -> falls back to asking approval.
Run modes Auto-review (classifier), Allowlist, Run Everything. Auto-review "is not a security boundary".

surprises: Cursor's current docs say it no longer stores embeddings for search, and forum posts say semantic indexing was turned down in favor of Instant Grep in 2026. The survey's key finding 4 (+12.5% with semantic search) describes a path Cursor has since retired.
Default read access is System: sandboxed commands can read outside the workspace unless Workspace mode is chosen.
Default network mode allows Cursor's built-in package-manager domains, not zero domains.
